# Accessibility in motion (house standards, version 4)

<!-- generated by tools/build_data.py from synthesis/; edit the source, not this file -->

Reduced motion, reduced transparency, increased contrast, text scaling, hover gating, touch targets and accessible overlays, shipped with the change and never as a follow-up.

Rules from non-negotiable sources. **must**: never break it without the person's explicit override. **should**: the default; say so when you depart from it. How to change one: `../standards.md`.

### STD-accessibility-motion-01: Ship reduced motion with the animation
**must**. Ship the prefers-reduced-motion variant of every animation that moves something (and, on the web, its hover gating) in the same change as the animation itself, including every prototype variant and every proposed motion recipe, never as a follow-up.
- Values: css: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); react: useReducedMotion(); react-native: useReducedMotion() or reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System
- Why: Animations can cause motion sickness, so reduced motion and hover gating ship with the animation every time; missing reduced-motion handling on movement is flagged on sight.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-016, S-L19-024, S-L19-031, S-L19-032, S-L19-023, S-L19-019, S-L19-015

### STD-accessibility-motion-02: Reduced motion is gentler, never zero
**must**. Under reduced motion, remove movement (translation, scale, slides, springs, parallax, elastic and overshoot) and replace it with a short opacity cross-fade (the sources use 200ms, ease) or a static transition, while keeping the opacity and color changes that explain a state change; never remove all animation or feedback.
- Values: remove: translation, scale, slides, springs, parallax, elastic, overshoot; keep: opacity and color changes that aid comprehension; cross-fade: 200ms ease; css-example: .element { animation: fade 0.2s ease; }; sheet-example: .sheet { transition: opacity 200ms ease; transform: none !important; }
- Why: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not zero: a gentler, non-vestibular equivalent that keeps the transitions that aid comprehension, not the removal of feedback.
- `engine.py review` checks it: This reset zeroes every animation under reduced motion; keep opacity and color changes (a fade on the motion.duration.reduced-fade token, var(--ds-motion-duration-reduced-fade)) and drop only movement.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-016, S-L19-020, S-L19-023, S-L19-025, S-L19-032, S-L19-033, S-L19-024

### STD-accessibility-motion-03: Branch JS motion values on reduced motion
**must** · react, react-native. In JavaScript-driven motion, read the reduced-motion setting (useReducedMotion(), or Reanimated's reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System on each animation) and swap movement values for static ones when it is on, for example closedX = reduce ? 0 : '-100%'.
- Values: react: const reduce = useReducedMotion(); const closedX = reduce ? 0 : '-100%';; react-native: const reduced = useReducedMotion(); const y = useSharedValue(reduced ? 0 : SHEET_HEIGHT); or withSpring(0, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System })
- Why: Reduced motion removes movement and position changes, and the sources' JS route is to read useReducedMotion() and branch the transform values on it.
- Sources: S-L19-025, S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-016

### STD-accessibility-motion-04: Native screen transitions fade when reduced
**must** · react-native. When reduced motion is on, switch native stack screen transitions to a crossfade: screenOptions={{ animation: reduced ? 'fade' : 'default' }}.
- Values: screenOptions: animation: reduced ? 'fade' : 'default'
- Why: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not zero, so screen transitions become animation: 'fade' instead of the push.
- Sources: S-L19-016, S-L19-015

### STD-accessibility-motion-05: Check reduced motion by toggling it
**must** · web. Put a reduced-motion step in the verification (feel check) of every motion change: toggle prefers-reduced-motion in DevTools' Rendering panel and confirm that movement is dropped while opacity feedback remains.
- Values: tool: Rendering panel: prefers-reduced-motion
- Why: It is a fixed line in the feel check of the implementation-plan template, and the source says the feel check is not optional: motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong.
- Sources: S-L19-026

### STD-accessibility-motion-06: Missing reduced motion blocks approval
**must**. In motion reviews and audits, rate movement without prefers-reduced-motion handling as a MEDIUM finding, also report reduced-motion code that removes all feedback, and approve a change only when reduced motion is respected.
- Values: severity: MEDIUM
- Why: The audit rates missing reduced-motion 'noticeably off' (MEDIUM) and hunts both failure modes; the review flags missing reduced-motion handling on movement on sight and lists 'reduced-motion respected' among the Approve criteria.
- Sources: S-L19-027, S-L19-025, S-L19-032

### STD-accessibility-motion-07: No full-viewport moving backgrounds
**should**. Do not put a moving background behind the full viewport.
- Why: The Apple design guidance lists full-viewport moving backgrounds among the motion to avoid in its reduced-motion and accessibility section, whose aim is a gentler, non-vestibular experience.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-08: No slow looping oscillations near 0.2 Hz
**should**. Do not loop a slow oscillation near 0.2 Hz (about one cycle every 5 seconds).
- Values: frequency: 0.2 Hz; period: one cycle per 5s
- Why: The Apple design guidance lists slow looping oscillations near 0.2 Hz among the motion to avoid in its reduced-motion and accessibility section.
- `engine.py review` checks it: An infinite loop of about one cycle every 5 seconds (0.2 Hz) is motion to avoid; drop the loop or make it faster and finite.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-09: Ease theme changes, no brightness jumps
**should**. Ease the switch between dark and light themes instead of letting brightness jump abruptly.
- Why: The Apple design guidance lists abrupt brightness jumps among the changes to avoid and says to ease dark/light theme changes.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-10: Soften large surfaces while they move
**should**. Make large moving objects semi-transparent while they travel, and during a large reposition fade big surfaces out and back in once they settle.
- Why: Part of the Apple design guidance for reduced motion and accessibility: large moving areas are softened rather than shown travelling at full strength.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-11: Reduced transparency makes surfaces solid
**must** · web, css. Handle prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce as its own signal, separate from reduced motion: make translucent surfaces frostier or solid by raising their background opacity and dropping the blur.
- Values: css: @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce); example: .toolbar { background: white; backdrop-filter: none; }
- Why: Components respond to three independent signals (reduced motion, reduced transparency, increased contrast), and each one gets its own treatment baked into the component.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-12: Increased contrast gets solid, bordered surfaces
**must** · web, css. Handle prefers-contrast: more as its own signal: give surfaces near-solid backgrounds with a defined, contrasting border.
- Values: css: @media (prefers-contrast: more)
- Why: It is one of the three independent signals the source says to bake into components.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-13: Scale layout with the user's text size
**must**. Respect the user's text-size setting (Dynamic Type) by scaling layout with the text; on the web write spacing in rem or em, not fixed px.
- Values: spacing-units: rem, em (not px)
- Why: So a larger font does not break the layout.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Write spacing in rem or em so the layout scales with the user's text size.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-15: Gate hover motion to fine pointers
**must** · web, css. Put every :hover animation (and, for mobile web, every :hover style) inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), with both conditions, in the same change as the hover, and leave :active press feedback ungated.
- Values: css: @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); tailwind-v4: the hover: variant already compiles to @media (hover: hover); tailwind-v3: future.hoverOnlyWhenSupported; press: :active (ungated)
- Why: Touch has no hover, so browsers fake one: the first tap applies :hover and leaves it there until the user taps elsewhere. (hover: hover) means the primary input can hover and (pointer: fine) rules out styluses and Android devices that claim hover; :active is a real press on touch, so it needs no gate.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-025, S-L19-032, S-L19-033, S-L19-028, S-L19-024, S-L19-014

### STD-accessibility-motion-16: Build overlays on accessible primitives
**must** · web, react. Build dialogs, drawers, popovers, dropdown menus, selects and tabs on an accessible primitive (base-ui, or Radix such as Radix Dialog and Radix Tabs) that handles focus management, focus trapping and dismissal, and command menus on cmdk; never hand-roll a <div>-based dropdown or dialog with manual focus handling.
- Values: primitives: base-ui (https://base-ui.com); radix: Radix Dialog (Vaul is built on it), Radix Tabs; command-menu: cmdk
- Why: Hand-rolling those is how you end up with a <div> dropdown and no focus management; the primitive makes the component accessible and handles focus trapping and dismissal.
- `engine.py review` checks it: A <div> with a dialog, menu or listbox role is a hand-built overlay; build it on base-ui (or Radix) so focus trapping and dismissal come with it.
- Sources: S-L19-029, S-L19-018, S-L19-005, S-L19-010

### STD-accessibility-motion-17: Hide decorative duplicate layers
**should** · web, react. When a component stacks a visual-only duplicate of its content (a clip-path overlay copy of tabs or of a button label), mark the duplicate's container aria-hidden and give any buttons inside it tabIndex={-1}.
- Values: container: aria-hidden; buttons: tabIndex={-1}
- Why: The duplicated layer is only visual and the real, focusable controls sit underneath; the source code does this without stating a reason, which is presumably to keep assistive technology and keyboard focus on the real controls [inferred].
- Sources: S-L19-010, S-L19-007

### STD-accessibility-motion-18: Prototype picker: accessible markup and focus
**must** · web. Build the prototype variant picker with its fixed accessible markup: <nav aria-label="Prototype variants">, aria-hidden="true" on the highlight and divider spans, aria-label="Replay animation (R)" on the icon-only replay button, exactly one item carrying data-active and aria-current="true", a :focus-visible outline of 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4) with outline-offset 2px, and transition: none on the highlight under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
- Values: nav: aria-label="Prototype variants"; decorative-spans: aria-hidden="true"; replay: aria-label="Replay animation (R)"; active-item: data-active + aria-current="true"; focus-visible: outline: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4); outline-offset: 2px; reduced-motion: .proto-picker[data-ready] .proto-picker-highlight { transition: none; }
- Why: The picker's appearance is not a design decision; it is the spec, copied verbatim so it always reads as harness chrome.
- Sources: S-L19-030

### STD-accessibility-motion-20: Never rely on haptics alone
**must**. Never make a haptic the only feedback for an action; pair it with a visual change that works on its own.
- Why: Haptics are off system-wide for many users and silent on most Android hardware, so the visual has to stand alone.
- Sources: S-L19-016

### STD-accessibility-motion-23: Keep the toaster labelled and reachable
**should** · react, web. Keep Sonner's accessibility defaults on: the toast container's ARIA label ('Notifications', localised through containerAriaLabel), the Alt+T hotkey that focuses the toaster area, and dismissible: true, setting dismissible: false only when the user must not be able to close that toast.
- Values: containerAriaLabel: Notifications; hotkey: ⌥/alt + T; dismissible: true
- Why: Sonner's API gives the toast container an ARIA label and a keyboard shortcut that focuses the toaster area, and with dismissible: false the user cannot dismiss the toast; keeping these defaults as the house default is a reading of the API reference [inferred].
- Sources: S-L19-091, S-L19-092, S-L19-021, S-L19-022

### STD-accessibility-motion-24: Never trap the user in an overlay
**must**. Give every screen and overlay a way out: keep drawers dismissible by outside click, Escape and drag by default, and if one must be non-dismissible, give it an explicit close control such as Drawer.Close [inferred].
- Values: drawer-default: dismissible: true; explicit-close: Drawer.Close
- Why: Every screen should answer 'How do I get out?'; never trap the user. A non-dismissible Vaul drawer blocks outside click, Escape and drag, and the docs' own demo can then only be closed by refreshing the page; pairing it with Vaul's Close part ('the button that closes the drawer') is our connection [inferred]. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
- Sources: S-L19-020, S-L19-093, S-L19-097

### STD-accessibility-motion-25: Controlled drawers still react to Escape
**should** · react. When a Vaul drawer is controlled with the open prop, also pass onOpenChange so the app reacts to Escape and outside clicks.
- Values: props: open + onOpenChange
- Why: onOpenChange is called when the open state changes, which the docs call useful for reacting to esc/outside clicks when the drawer is controlled. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
- Sources: S-L19-094

### STD-accessibility-motion-26: Cover the inert page behind a drawer
**should** · web, react. While a modal drawer or sheet is open, render its overlay so a layer covers the inert rest of the view.
- Values: vaul: <Drawer.Overlay />
- Why: Vaul's Overlay is the layer that covers the inert portion of the view when the drawer is open, and a modal task pairs its surface with a dimming scrim. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
- Sources: S-L19-093, S-L19-020

### STD-accessibility-motion-27: Never disable pinch zoom
**must** · web. Never set user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 in the viewport meta tag; when the page zooms into an input, fix the input's font size (16px at the minimum) instead.
- Values: forbidden: user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1; input-font-size: 16px at the minimum
- Why: user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 are accessibility failures; the zoom they are used to stop comes from iOS Safari zooming into inputs under 16px, so the font size is the thing to fix.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Disabling zoom is an accessibility failure; remove it and set inputs to at least 16px so iOS does not zoom into them.
- Sources: S-L19-028
